title: probabilistic-eligibility-and-kv-tiered-eviction-for-surge-mitigation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Under sustained high QPS we observe recurring tail-latency spikes and GPU OOMs caused by microbatch admission oversubscription and KV cache hotspots. This ticket implements a probabilistic microbatch eligibility controller plus a KV-tiered eviction/soft-spill strategy to reduce synchronous GPU memory reclamation and provide graceful backpressure.

Goals:
- Prevent abrupt GPU memory pressure leading to failed requests or high latencies.
- Reduce amplification of bursts by smoothing admission while preserving throughput.
- Prioritize KV cache residency by request criticality (token locality + model affinity).
- Provide observable safety valves and an incremental rollout path.

Design overview:
1) Probabilistic Eligibility Gate: introduce a per-worker admission probability p(t) computed from a short-window estimator of
   - current GPU memory occupancy (including estimated KV residency),
   - pending microbatch queue length, and
   - observed request arrival rate (EWMA).
   p(t) maps to [0.0,1.0]; requests are accepted into the microbatch with probability p(t). The mapping is shaped to be conservative near hard headroom thresholds and permissive when headroom is ample.

   Key properties: jitter-avoiding: add a small deterministic offset based on request priority to avoid synchronized probabilistic rejections across workers. Priority tags derive from route and model (and customer tier).

2) KV-tiered eviction and soft-spill: instead of immediate KV eviction across the board on pressure, we introduce three KV tiers: HOT (active prefixes), WARM (recently used), COLD (rare). Eviction order is COLD -> WARM -> HOT. On sustained pressure we attempt soft-spill of WARM items to host memory or compressed quantized store rather than immediate eviction, preserving hit-rate for common prefixes while freeing GPU-resident KV for active requests.

3) Admission signals + gradual backpressure: admission probability p(t) reduces smoothly over a configurable hysteresis window (default 250ms ramp) so that upstream clients see gradual latencies rather than hard rejections. We keep a short token-bucket fallback to reject low-priority requests deterministically if p(t) falls below a floor.

4) Hotspot detection: use per-key access counters with decay to detect KV hotspots; when a small fraction of keys account for >X% of hits we mark the worker as "hotspot mode" and increase soft-spill aggressiveness while lifting admission probability slightly for requests referencing HOT keys to preserve QoS for those flows.

Metrics we will track:
- microbatch acceptance rate (p(t) observed vs configured)
- GPU memory headroom percentile (p50/p90/p99)
- KV hit-rate by tier and global hit-rate delta after soft-spill
- request latency P50/P95/P99 by priority and by hotspot flag
- failed requests / OOMs / retried requests

Safety and fallbacks:
- hard OOM guard: if free GPU memory < 100MB, immediate global reject to protect the worker and trigger fallback routing.
- audit logging: every probabilistic reject emits a lightweight event with reason, priority, and headroom snapshot for offline analysis.
- feature flagged rollout with canary ratio and rollout escalation criteria.

Implementation notes:
- controller implemented inside the admission controller (worker side) for minimal cross-node coordination. Use shared EWMA signal sources already present in runtime.
- KV-tier metadata stored as compact bloom-ish counters with epoch decay to be GPU memory friendly. Soft-spill uses a compact compressed format on host with LZ4 and optional int8 quantization for KV vectors.
- expand existing metrics to include per-tier residency and spontaneous spill counter.

Trade-offs considered:
- Probabilistic admits increase variance for single requests, but across high QPS this smooths load and prevents synchronized spikes. We mitigate variance for high-priority routes via deterministic offsets.
- Soft-spill adds host memory and CPU pressure; we mitigate by limiting spill bandwidth and using a background recycler with rate limits.

Acceptance criteria:
- No increase in P95 latency across top 10 production routes during canary at 10% traffic.
- 50% reduction in GPU OOMs induced by KV eviction under synthetic surge tests (see perf deck).
- KV global hit-rate drop < 3% after soft-spill when configured conservatively.
- Observable, auditable probabilistic-reject events and dashboards in console.

Rollout plan: see rollout_plan field below.

Artifacts: design doc (drive), perf harness (GH), dashboards (console).
comments: 2026-02-26 — Initial spike analysis attached: drive.google.com/drive/fake/design-doc (Aisha). Observed 3x increase in microbatch queue depth during 30s bursts leading to 2x headroom churn.
2026-03-02 — Sync with SRE: suggested lower default hysteresis to 200–300ms to avoid oscillation (Ethan Kim). Added hard OOM guard requirement.

2026-03-05 — Prototype admission controller implemented on branch feature/prob-admit. Local cluster test shows smoothing of acceptance rate with p(t) clamp. PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pulls/4312 (Marco).

2026-03-08 — PM feedback (Sofia Hernandez): ensure customer-impact tagging for low-priority rejections + include rollout gating for Dedicated customers. Added priority tag propagation to gateway headers.
2026-03-11 — Load test 1 (10k RPS synthetic): GPU OOMs down 60% vs baseline; KV hit-rate dropped 1.8% with conservative spill. Need extended test at 40k RPS to validate hotspot behavior (Marco).
2026-03-13 — Design review notes: add observability for per-worker hotspot boolean, and a debug switch to force-tier promotion/demotion for repro (reviewers: Lian Zhou, Priya Rao).
acceptance_criteria: Canary at 10% shows no P95 regression for top 10 routes
Synthetic surge test shows >=50% drop in GPU OOMs caused by KV eviction
KV hit-rate drop <=3% with conservative default configuration
Probabilistic rejects are logged and visible in console with headroom snapshot
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal QA on staging cluster with synthetic surge harness (week 1)
Phase 1: Canary rollout 1% -> 10% for non-dedicated hosted customers (week 2)
Phase 2: Expand canary to 25% with dedicated-only opt-in for Dedicated customers (week 3)
Phase 3: Global rollout with tuned defaults and runtime flags enabled (week 4)
Rollback criteria: sustained P95 increase >5% for critical routes or unexplained OOMs
